name: Asti
title: Asti Palio, Moscato d'Asti Vineyards & Monferrato Heritage Host
worldview: Defiance must be sweet and celebrated on horseback. We have run our medieval bareback horse race—the Palio—since 1275, directly under the nose of our rival city-states, and we ferment our sparkling Moscato to preserve the fresh, floral scent of the grape, proving that our freedom is a sweet, long-lasting celebration. We run on the wind.

learning_objectives: Understand the rise of the independent commune of Asti in the Middle Ages and the historical significance of the Palio (the oldest continuously run race in Italy).
Analyze the cold-fermentation chemistry (Asti method) used to produce Moscato d'Asti, explaining how stopping fermentation early preserves natural grape sugars and low alcohol.
Evaluate the UNESCO cultural landscape of the Monrate, Langhe, and Roero hills as models of traditional viticultural systems.
discussion_prompts: Why did the medieval communes of northern Italy use violent, public horse races (Palio) to perform and settle territorial and aristocratic rivalries?

How does the Asti method of fermentation, which stops the yeast from converting all the sugar to alcohol, manage to preserve the fresh, volatile aroma of the Muscat grape better than traditional dry wine methods?
How do the family-run contrade (districts) of Asti maintain their social and historical cohesion in a modern, digital city?
